title: The engine and the providers
dek: Terraform's intermediate representation is a dependency graph, and its back end is somebody else's process. This part follows one plan from a loaded configuration through Terraform v1.17.0's engine: the 31 transformers that build a resource-level graph, the walker that gives every vertex a goroutine and skips only what depends on a failure, instances that appear only at walk time, the per-instance plan in which the provider proposes and core decides, providers as child processes reached through a one-line handshake, the 36-RPC wire contract and its msgpack values, and the apply that re-plans rather than replays the saved plan.
byline: 24 October 2026 · Subject: terraform@018a99c8 (v1.17.0) · Part 2 of 4 · Read from the source; measured on this machine with no cloud credentials
description: Terraform v1.17.0's engine and provider protocol read from the source: the plan-graph transformer pipeline, the DAG walker and -parallelism, count/for_each expansion, the per-instance plan and -minimal-refresh, provider processes and the go-plugin handshake, tfplugin6 and cty msgpack on the wire, saved plan files and the apply re-plan. Part 2 of Terraform, taken apart.
og_description: Part 2 of Terraform, taken apart. 31 transformers build a graph with no instance nodes; a goroutine per vertex walks it and a failure skips only dependents; -parallelism guards Execute only; a trivial plan starts its provider three times and a three-cloud plan eighteen; tfplugin6 has 36 RPCs and a label that stopped tracking them; apply re-plans every instance and checks it against the saved plan.
twitter_description: Terraform's graph builder, walker, provider processes, wire protocol and plan files, read from v1.17.0 and measured with no cloud credentials. Part 2 of Terraform, taken apart.
badges_callout:
How to read the badges

from the code marks a fact read from hashicorp/terraform at 018a99c83c5d (tag v1.17.0, 21 October 2026), cited as a path and line range from the repository root. Other repositories carry a prefix: go-plugin v1.7.0 (92fb14e530db), terraform-plugin-go v0.31.0 (09a1181b051c), go-cty at a918e1174fca (Terraform pins v1.18.1; equivalence of the cited lines is not verified) and terraform-plugin-framework at 00badb1b0584. measured here marks a count, byte dump or behaviour observed with the v1.17.0 binary on a 2-vCPU Linux box, with the providers aws 6.70.0, google 8.8.0, azurerm 5.10.0 and random 3.9.1 from a shared plugin cache. No cloud credentials existed. Nothing was applied to a cloud: plans that needed a cloud provider used fake credentials, and the engine experiments used only random and terraform_data. Timings depend on page cache and load, so they are given as ranges. reconstruction marks a judgement drawn from those sources rather than read in one place.

This is Part 2 of 4 of Terraform, taken apart. Part 1 covers the HCL language, values and how init turns a directory into a configuration tree. Part 3 covers the state file, locks, refactoring blocks and the 1.5 → 1.17 feature arc. Part 4 builds one project on AWS, GCP and Azure with no credentials and places Terraform in its ecosystem.
